tests.name: BMI lookup
tests.message: Find variables related to BMI
tests.pass: search proposed (contains body mass index) and no query; short prose names `\Nhanes\examination\body measures\Body Mass Index (kg per m**2)\` with its exact path. The proposed search holds no term that matched nothing (no bare bmi).

tests.name: Typo + obesity measures
tests.message: show me variables for body mas index and other obesity measures
tests.pass: search proposed covering BMI and at least two of height, weight, waist; prose summarizes them with exact paths; no query. No search is PARTIAL. If the reply says the variables are shown/displayed in the results table, a search must have been proposed; a claim with no search is a FAIL. Flag duplicated reply text.

tests.name: Cholesterol research
tests.message: My research is on cholesterol levels across different demographic groups. What variables should I look at?
tests.pass: cholesterol (total, HDL, LDL) AND demographics (sex, age, race/ethnicity), grouped, exact paths; no query. A search proposal is optional (note it).

tests.name: Labs / missing data
tests.message: I'm interested in creatinine, albumin, leukocytes, and d dimer. Are these available? Also, can I study sickle cell disease?
tests.pass: creatinine and albumin found; leukocytes mapped to white blood cell count; D-dimer and sickle cell reported not available (unless the env's dictionary now has them); nothing invented; no query. A search proposal for the found labs is optional (note it).

tests.name: Cohort query proposal
tests.message: Show me female participants over 40 and include their BMI
tests.pass: SEX [female], AGE min 40 (a max at or above 85 is noted, not failed), select has BMI + SEX + AGE; query returned; no search, no facets; prose without JSON. A reply with no query is a FAIL. If the log has "checking the counted query", the counted-query guard supplied it: note it, and check the returned query matches what was counted.

tests.name: "Show me" is a lookup
tests.message: Just show me BMI and waist circumference
tests.pass: search proposed covering both (e.g. `body mass index | waist circumference`); no query; prose names both with exact paths. The proposed search must find BMI: body mass index in it, no bare BMI.

tests.name: Narrowing follow-up
tests.message: narrow that to people over 50
tests.pass: SEX kept, AGE min becomes 50, select still has BMI + SEX + AGE; query returned; no search, no facets. A model removeSelect is a FAIL.

tests.name: Select with no filters
tests.message: Select all race variables
tests.pass: search proposed (contains race); no query; prose names `\Nhanes\demographics\RACE\`. A select-only propose_query is read as the search that found the variables, so there should be NO refused propose_query (error=true) in the log; count any. A reply saying the variables are now selected/added to the selection is a FAIL (the propose_query result says nothing was selected).

tests.name: Select with existing filters
tests.message: Select all race variables
tests.pass: query returned keeping SEX and AGE filters; select has RACE + SEX + AGE + BMI; no search. BMI dropped from select is a FAIL (only removeSelect removes a variable). The model adds both race paths with addSelect; a flagged plain select is a note, not a FAIL.

tests.name: Lookup from the UI's empty query
tests.message: Select all race variables
tests.pass: same as T10; no 400.

tests.name: Cohort from the UI's empty query
tests.message: Show me female participants over 40 and include their BMI
tests.pass: same as T7; no 400.

tests.name: Several topics in one question
tests.message: Do you have anything on smoking, alcohol use, sleep, and physical activity?
tests.pass: each topic answered (smoking and alcohol with exact paths, physical activity found); sleep is found as three Synthea G47 sleep-disorder paths, so it must be reported with them, not as not found; alcohol lists all seven: the four `\Nhanes\questionnaire\alcohol use\` items (days drink in year, drink 5 in a day, drink per day, days 5 drinks in year), `food component recall\Alcohol (gm)`, `supplement use\ALCOHOL_PERCENT`, and the Synthea F10 path; short summary, not the full smoking list; no query; finishes under the cap. A search is expected (model-called, or added by the service because one search found the named paths); no search is PARTIAL. Any path flag is a FAIL for that path. A topic with about eight or fewer matches written as "examples include" is a FAIL. Paths left out of the prose are still a FAIL for the prose, but note that the table would show them. An "asking the model to correct them" log line means the path repair ran; note whether the final reply still has a flagged path (FAIL) or was fixed. Note the search terms used in any failing run.

tests.name: Remove a selected variable
tests.message: Remove BMI from my selected variables
tests.pass: query returned with SEX and AGE filters kept; select has SEX + AGE and no BMI; the model sends removeSelect with BMI. The reply says BMI is removed only if it was; a reply claiming a removal the returned query does not show is a FAIL.

tests.name: Browse by category
tests.message: Show me all the laboratory variables
tests.pass: list_facets called; no query. list_facets returns categories (dataset_id, data_type) but none for laboratory, so a search for laboratory is proposed; nothing guessed, and no facet that list_facets did not return. Any offer to narrow by dataset or data type must be a real category. Flag a proposal that lists non-laboratory matches (Labetalol, laborer) as laboratory variables.

tests.name: Topic within a dataset
tests.message: Show me the cholesterol variables in the NHANES dataset
tests.pass: list_facets called, search_concepts called with the facet {category: dataset_id, name: Nhanes}, and the response carries search containing cholesterol AND facets [{dataset_id, Nhanes}]; no query. The prose names only NHANES cholesterol paths and no Synthea ones (the narrowed search returns six). If the reply says the variables are shown/displayed in the results table, a search must have been proposed; a claim with no search is a FAIL. A facet that list_facets did not return is a FAIL. Flag duplicated reply text.

tests.name: Alcohol on its own
tests.message: What alcohol variables do you have?
tests.pass: names all six local paths: the four `\Nhanes\questionnaire\alcohol use\` items, `food component recall\Alcohol (gm)`, `supplement use\ALCOHOL_PERCENT` (plus the Synthea F10 path in the target env); exact paths; no query. A search containing alcohol is expected; no search is PARTIAL. If this passes while T14 fails, the cause is the combined search crowding the page; if it fails too, the dictionary search is not returning them. Note the search terms used in any failing run.

tests.name: Facet-only browse
tests.message: Show me all the continuous variables
tests.pass: list_facets called; the response carries facets [{data_type, continuous}] copied from list_facets, with or without a search; no query. Prose gives the count or a few examples with exact paths, not the whole list; nothing guessed.

tests.name: Replace a selected variable
tests.message: Replace BMI with weight
tests.pass: query returned keeping SEX and AGE filters; select has Weight (kg) + SEX + AGE and NO BMI; no search; the model sends addSelect with Weight (kg) and removeSelect with BMI. BMI still in select is a FAIL, and so is a reply claiming the replacement when the returned query still has BMI.

tests.name: Count question is not a query change
tests.message: How many female participants over 40 are there?
tests.pass: count_participants called; prose gives the count as obfuscated, not exact; NO query returned (the counted-query guard must not fire on a plain count question; a "checking the counted query" log line is a FAIL unless the reply really claimed the query changed, then note the wording). A search is acceptable.

tests.name: Model sends only the selection change
tests.message: Select all race variables
tests.pass: Same request as T11, run 5 times and scored on what the model sent. Count each flag: "did not add" (a race path missing from addSelect), "removed ... unasked" (any removeSelect: BMI would be dropped), and "sent select (read as addSelect)" (still using the old field; works, but note how often). The returned query must keep SEX and AGE and have RACE + SEX + AGE + BMI, as in T11.

tests.name: Exclusion is a filter, not a removal
tests.message: Exclude smokers from my cohort
tests.pass: query returned keeping SEX and AGE filters and adding a smoking filter that excludes smokers (not: true on a smoking variable, or the non-smoker values of a categorical one, from a search this turn); select still has BMI + SEX + AGE, plus the smoking variable the filter adds; no removeSelect (flagged "removed ... unasked" is a FAIL). Note the smoking path and how the exclusion was written.
